The tape exits from the central cavity over a short front bridge into the cutter assembly; the open cavity is a deliberate negative space, not a surface decal.

research_questions.question: Is the C38 body one continuous wedge or a separate top shell over a weighted lower base, and where do the cavity, front cutter face, and tape bridge meet it?
research_questions.trigger: A generic tape-dispenser silhouette would hide the actual C38's part boundaries and negative space.

candidates.observed_identity: Scotch C38 Classic Desktop Tape Dispenser
candidates.reason: Official image establishes the loaded body/cavity/cutter relationship and is consistent with the official dimensions and functional description.
The unloaded image reveals the cavity, hub placement, bridge, cutter, and lower seam that are obscured by tape in the official photo.

research_questions.resolution: Treat the outer body as a main box-derived upper shell plus a visibly separate weighted lower base. Preserve the open longitudinal cavity and model the removable hub and metal cutting blade as distinct assemblies.
